readout_other: Functional ultrasound CBV imaging of S1HL (40 MHz), resting-state functional connectivity, von Frey testing, paw motion video analysis
direction_notes: FUS to the sciatic nerve evoked paw movement and increased CBV in contralateral hind-limb S1; in spared nerve injury mice FUS stabilised the CBV rise to repeated electrical stimulation, a trend that did not reach significance.

exposures.label: FUS to the sciatic nerve (3.1 MHz)

timing.protocol_description: One 1 ms FUS pulse per muscle activation; wild-type mice received a train of 5 pulses at 1 Hz, neuropathic pain mice a 10 Hz train for 10 s delivered during paired electrical paw stimulation.

source_quotes.n_subjects: For experiments with wild-type mice: n = 10 total (n = 2 whisker stimulation, n = 3 electric paw stimulation, n = 3 FUS stimulation, n = 2 FUS + electrical stimulation).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: FUS was performed using a 3.1 MHz focused transducer.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: To elicit a compound muscle activation, one single 1 ms, 9.57 MPa derated rarefactional pressure FUS pulse was delivered to the sciatic nerve non-invasively.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: To elicit a compound muscle activation, one single 1 ms, 9.57 MPa derated rarefactional pressure FUS pulse was delivered to the sciatic nerve non-invasively.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Once positioning was sufficient to elicit robust and continuous neuromodulation, a train of 5 pulses using the previously defined parameters at 1 Hz was used during the fUS imaging experiments (Supplemental Video S4). For neuropathic pain mice, PRF was increased to 10 Hz and the sonication duration to 10 s (0.1% DC effective).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: FUS sonication parameters (9.57 MPa (derated), 10 Hz, 10 seconds, 1% DC)
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Once positioning was sufficient to elicit robust and continuous neuromodulation, a train of 5 pulses using the previously defined parameters at 1 Hz was used during the fUS imaging experiments (Supplemental Video S4). For neuropathic pain mice, PRF was increased to 10 Hz and the sonication duration to 10 s (0.1% DC effective).
